title: Should Playing the Piano Hurt? No — and Here Is What Hurting Means
summary: It should not hurt. Not at your age, not at any age, not even at the beginning. If it does, it is information — and it is usually about four specific things.

title: The Bass Clef Is Not Harder — It Is Just Later
summary: Adults tell me the bass clef is the hard one. It is not harder. You have simply seen it a tenth as often, and there is a fix for that.

title: Coming Back to the Piano After Twenty Years Away
summary: You are not starting from nothing, whatever it feels like in the first week. But you are also not starting from where you left off, and knowing the difference saves a year.

title: Learning Piano Without a Teacher: What You Can and Cannot Diagnose Alone
summary: Most of learning the piano can now be done alone, and done well. Four specific things cannot — and knowing which four is the whole difference.

title: How to Sit at the Piano: Bench Height, Distance, and Why It Decides Everything
summary: It is the least interesting subject in music and the one that quietly decides how you will sound. Three minutes, once, and most of the usual problems never arrive.

title: How Long Before I Can Play a Real Piece?
summary: A specific answer rather than an encouraging one — including what “a real piece” turns out to mean once you are inside it.

title: 61, 76 or 88 Keys: What You Can and Cannot Play on Each
summary: A straight answer about key counts — what runs out, when it runs out, and the question that matters considerably more than this one.

title: Reading Music or Playing by Ear: Which Should an Adult Learn First?
summary: Adults are told to pick a side. Both camps are describing something real — and for a beginner the answer is far less dramatic than the argument.

title: You Can Play All the Right Notes and It Still Sounds Wrong
summary: You have the notes. You have the rhythm. And it still does not sound like music. This is the most common thing adults describe to me, and it has a specific cause.

title: Learning Piano After 70: What Changes, What Does Not
summary: Some things really are different, and pretending otherwise helps nobody. Most of the important ones are not, and that is the part people are not told.

title: The Plateau: Why Month Four Feels Like Going Backwards
summary: It arrives at around the same time for almost everyone, it feels like proof that you have no talent, and it is in fact a specific and well-understood thing.

title: Why You Freeze When Someone Listens
summary: You have played it forty times alone and it was fine. Someone walks into the room and your hands are suddenly not yours. There are reasons, and there are things that work.

title: How to Run Your Own Piano Lesson When You Do Not Have a Teacher
summary: Most of what a teacher does in an hour, you can do for yourself once you know what the hour is supposed to contain. One part you cannot, and it is worth knowing which.

title: Adults Learn Piano Differently From Children — and Mostly Better
summary: The comparison is always made in one direction. Having taught both for years, I think the balance is considerably more even than adults are told.

title: How to Practice Piano in an Apartment Without Annoying Anyone
summary: A surprising share of adults stop playing for a reason that has nothing to do with the piano: they are worried about being heard.

title: How to Choose a Piece You Will Actually Finish
summary: The piece you choose decides more about whether you keep playing than how much you practice does.

title: Why Your Hands Will Not Do Two Different Things at Once
summary: Every pianist starts with the hands coupled. What separates a player who can do it from one who cannot is not the brain they were born with — it is a specific kind of practice.

title: Why You Still Cannot Read Music Fluently — and What Actually Fixes It
summary: Naming notes and reading music are two different skills. Months of practice at the first one will not produce the second, and almost nobody is told the difference.

title: Those Little Numbers Above the Notes Are Not Suggestions
summary: A fingering is a plan for the whole phrase, not a preference about one note. Ignoring it is what puts a permanent stumble in the middle of a piece that is not actually difficult.

title: When Should You Start Using the Pedal? And How to Stop It Sounding Like Mud
summary: The pedal is not a sustain button. It is a second instrument played with your foot, and it has its own technique — starting with the fact that the foot moves after the hand, never with it.

title: Counting Out Loud Feels Childish. Do It Anyway.
summary: Nobody hears you. And the thing counting fixes is the thing a listener notices first — long before they notice a wrong note.

title: "Play It Musically" — What That Actually Means, in Practical Terms
summary: Your ear already knows what beautiful sounds like. The gap is not taste — it is that nobody has told you which physical movements produce it.

title: The Left Hand Is Not the Weak Hand
summary: You have spent forty years doing fine work with one hand and carrying things with the other. That is training history, not anatomy, and it can be corrected on purpose.

title: Two Staves, One Instrument: How to Read the Grand Staff Without Getting Lost
summary: The two staves are not two pieces of music side by side. They are one keyboard, cut in half at middle C, and reading them is a skill with its own practice.

title: What the Time Signature Is Actually Telling You
summary: It is not a fraction and it is not decoration. It tells you how to count, and counting is what holds playing together.

title: How to Keep Playing Through a Week When Nothing Is Normal
summary: The adults who lose months are almost never the ones who missed four days. They are the ones who decided that missing four days meant they had stopped.

title: Should You Learn Scales? Yes — but Not for the Reason You Were Told
summary: Not discipline, not finger strength, not because they are good for you. There are three specific things a scale teaches that pieces do not teach efficiently.

title: Two Notes at Once: How to Make the Top One Sing
summary: This is the difference between a chord that sounds like a block and a chord that sounds like music with a melody on top of it.

title: What Piano or Keyboard Should You Buy to Start? What Actually Matters
summary: One requirement is structural and everything else is preference. Adults put off starting for months over a decision that is simpler than the listings make it look.

title: How to Practice a Piece You Cannot Play Yet
summary: Playing and practicing are two different activities. Nobody tells you the difference when you learn alone, and it is the reason an hour of work leaves the difficult passage exactly as difficult.

title: What Sharps and Flats Actually Do (and Why One Key Has Two Names)
summary: The rule takes ten seconds to learn. What nobody tells adult beginners is how long a sharp stays in force, and why F sharp and G flat are the same key with two names.

title: Why Chord Changes Feel Impossible — and the Practice That Fixes Them
summary: The problem is almost never speed. It is that you are moving five fingers when the music only asked you to move one.

title: What a Metronome Is Actually For (It Is Not Making You Play Faster)
summary: A metronome does not make you play faster. It shows you where your playing is uneven — which is uncomfortable, and is exactly the information you need.

title: How to Memorize a Piece of Music: The Four Kinds of Memory
summary: If your hands know a piece but you cannot start it from the middle, you have one kind of memory and you need four.

title: Why You Stop Every Time You Make a Mistake (and How to Stop Stopping)
summary: Nobody decides to do this. It happens by itself, it feels responsible, and it quietly builds a piece that has a perfect opening and no ending.

title: Easy Christmas Carols for Adult Beginners (and How to Make Them Sound Finished)
summary: You do not need more notes to sound better. You need the notes you have to be shaped — and carols are the easiest place to learn how.

title: How to Tell If You Are Actually Improving at the Piano
summary: The things that improve first are not the things you are watching. That is why so many adults conclude they are stuck a month before it shows.

title: What a Piano Teacher Hears in Your Playing That You Do Not
summary: Adults learning alone check for wrong notes, because wrong notes are the only fault they have a name for. A teacher is listening to something else entirely.

title: You Got a Keyboard for Christmas. Now What?
summary: The first week decides whether the instrument becomes a habit or a piece of furniture. Almost none of what matters is about the keyboard itself.

title: Piano Goals for the New Year That You Will Actually Keep
summary: "Practice every day" and "learn Clair de Lune" are the two commonest resolutions, and they fail in opposite ways.

title: What the First Year of Piano Actually Looks Like
summary: Not a promise and not a syllabus — a description, so you can tell whether what is happening to you is normal. Usually it is.

title: What to Practice on a Day You Do Not Feel Like Practicing
summary: Not a motivation lecture. One specific, small thing to do on the days when sitting down at the piano feels like too much.

title: How to Practice Slowly Without It Becoming Meaningless
summary: “Practice it slowly” is the most-repeated advice in music and the least explained. There is a right way to do it, and most adults are not doing it.

title: How Loud Is Loud? p, mf and f, Explained Practically
summary: There is no decibel value for forte. What there is, is a relationship — and once you see it, the markings stop being guesswork.

title: How to Start Sight-Reading: A Method You Can Begin This Week
summary: You do not get better at reading by learning pieces. You get better by reading things you will never learn.

title: What Is a Key Signature, and Why Does It Change?
summary: A key signature is a labor-saving device. Understanding what it is doing makes it far less intimidating than it looks.

title: A Five-Minute Warm-Up That Is Actually Worth Doing
summary: A warm-up is not practice and it is not an exercise. Its whole job is to get the hand and the ear ready, and that takes five minutes.

title: Finger Independence: What Helps, and What Quietly Causes Injury
summary: Some of the best-known finger exercises in piano history have injured more hands than they have helped. The anatomy explains why.

title: Reading Ledger Lines Without Counting Every Time
summary: Those little extra lines are not a new alphabet. Two landmarks and one habit turn them into notes you recognize.

title: Why You Cannot Play Fast Yet (It Is Not Your Fingers)
summary: Adults assume speed comes with strength or youth. It comes from efficiency of movement, and here is what is eating yours.

title: Andante, Allegro, Moderato: What Tempo Markings Actually Mean
summary: Beginners look up Allegro, find a number, and set the metronome. That is not quite what the word is for.

title: Arpeggios: What They Are and Why They Feel Impossible at First
summary: If arpeggios feel lumpy and uneven no matter how slowly you go, you are almost certainly missing one specific motion.

title: When Should You Move On From a Piece?
summary: You do not have to finish a piece to have learned from it. Knowing when to let one go is a skill of its own.

title: Repeat Signs, D.C., Coda: How to Find Your Way Through a Piece
summary: Da capo, dal segno, the coda sign, first and second endings — these are directions, not music, and they are simpler than they look.
